evals.name: readme-from-project
evals.prompt: Write a README.md for the tidyfeed project in evals/files/tidyfeed/. It's going on GitHub soon and people need to know what it is and how to get going with it.
evals.expected_output: A README built from the project's real facts: what tidyfeed does and why to use it before any tech stack, who it's for, install and token setup that match pyproject.toml and config.py, only real commands and flags, Apache-2.0 license, and no template scaffolding.
expectations: The README describes what tidyfeed does and why someone would use it before it mentions Python, requests, or other implementation technologies
The README states who the project is for (its intended users)
The README gives install steps that use pip and states the Python 3.14 or later requirement
The README explains how to provide the API token: the TIDYFEED_TOKEN environment variable or the token key in ~/.config/tidyfeed/config.toml
The README states the license as Apache-2.0
[script] No TGDP template placeholders or boilerplate remain
[script] Every tidyfeed subcommand and flag shown exists in tidyfeed/cli.py
[script] No invented project URLs (repo, package index, or tidyfeed hosts) unless marked TODO
[script] No invented TIDYFEED_* environment variables

evals.name: howto-rotate-token
evals.prompt: Users of tidyfeed (project is in evals/files/tidyfeed/) keep asking us how to rotate the API token it uses. Write them a doc for that.
evals.expected_output: A how-to (not a tutorial or concept page): one goal, numbered steps that start with verbs, create the new token before revoking the old one, update whichever token location is in use, verify with check-token, then revoke the old token.
expectations: The doc is a goal-focused how-to for the single task of rotating the token, not a tutorial that teaches by building something or a conceptual explainer
The procedure is a numbered (ordered) list, and any step that only applies in some cases starts with its condition ("If …, then …")
The doc says to create the new token (Settings > API tokens) before revoking the old one
The doc covers both token locations and that TIDYFEED_TOKEN takes precedence over the config file token
The doc uses tidyfeed check-token to verify the new token before revoking the old one
[script] No TGDP template placeholders or boilerplate remain
[script] Every tidyfeed subcommand and flag shown exists in tidyfeed/cli.py
[script] No invented project URLs (repo, package index, or tidyfeed hosts) unless marked TODO
[script] No invented TIDYFEED_* environment variables

evals.name: release-notes-from-log
evals.prompt: We just tagged tidyfeed 2.0.0. Write the release notes for it from evals/files/tidyfeed/git-log-2.0.txt (the rest of the project is in that folder too if you need it).
evals.expected_output: User-facing release notes: breaking changes called out with what users must do, new features and fixes described in user terms, internal-only commits (CI, tests, refactors, release chores) left out, no commit hashes.
expectations: Breaking changes are called out separately from other changes and include all three: --max-items renamed to --limit, ~/.tidyfeedrc support dropped, Python 3.14 or later required
Each breaking change tells users what to do to upgrade
New features include markdown export, the check-token command, and the TIDYFEED_TOKEN environment variable
Both bug fixes are described in user terms: duplicate items when feeds share a URL, and CSV export failing on items without a published date
[script] No TGDP template placeholders or boilerplate remain
[script] No commit hashes appear
[script] No internal-only commits (CI, tests, refactors, release chores) are listed
[script] Every tidyfeed subcommand and flag shown exists in tidyfeed/cli.py, apart from the removed --max-items

evals.name: review-readme-draft
evals.prompt: Is this README missing anything? evals/files/tidyfeed/README-draft.md — the project it's for is in the same folder.
evals.expected_output: A review, not a silent rewrite: identifies the doc as a README, reports the gaps ranked by reader impact, grounded in the project's real facts.
expectations: The response presents its findings before, or instead of, a full rewritten README
The findings are ranked or prioritised by impact on the reader
It flags that the description leads with technologies instead of what tidyfeed does and why to use it
It flags the missing statement of who the project is for
It flags missing installation steps or prerequisites (Python 3.14+, installing with pip)
It flags that the config section lacks specifics, such as TIDYFEED_TOKEN, the config file path, or config.example.toml

evals.name: tutorial-first-reading-list
evals.prompt: We'd like a tutorial for people who have never used tidyfeed (it's in evals/files/tidyfeed/). Have them learn how it works by building a Markdown reading list from a couple of blogs they follow.
evals.expected_output: A learning-oriented tutorial: says what the reader will learn and who it's for, lists what they need first, follows one path that builds the reading list end to end in tidyfeed's real order, shows the result of key steps, and ends with a summary and next steps.
expectations: The doc is a tutorial that teaches by building one concrete result (a Markdown reading list), not a reference page or a bare list of commands
It states up front what the reader will learn or be able to do, and who the tutorial is for
It lists what the reader needs before starting: Python 3.14 or later, and a Tidyfeed account or API token (creating the token in a later step counts)
The steps follow tidyfeed's real dependencies: the token is set before check-token, feeds are configured before fetch, and fetch runs before export --format markdown
At least two steps show or describe what the reader should see when the step works (for example 'token OK' or 'fetched N items')
It ends with a summary of what the reader built or learned and points to next steps
[script] No TGDP template placeholders or boilerplate remain
[script] Every tidyfeed subcommand and flag shown exists in tidyfeed/cli.py
[script] No invented project URLs (repo, package index, or tidyfeed hosts) unless marked TODO
[script] No invented TIDYFEED_* environment variables

evals.name: choose-doc-type-mixed-request
evals.prompt: For tidyfeed (evals/files/tidyfeed/), we want ONE doc that gets brand-new users to their first export in under two minutes AND documents every command and option in full. What should we write?
evals.expected_output: Advice, not a combined doc: recognises two different reader goals, recommends a quickstart (or getting-started doc) and a reference, explains why one doc would serve both readers poorly, and grounds the plan in tidyfeed's real commands.
expectations: It identifies that the request combines two different reader goals: the fastest path to a first result, and complete lookup of every command and option
It recommends separate docs and names both types: a quickstart (or getting-started doc) and a reference
It explains why a single doc would serve both readers poorly
Its recommendation is two separate docs. Drafting both, or mentioning a single-file fallback, is fine as long as the fallback isn't the recommendation
Its plan uses tidyfeed's real commands, for example fetch, export and check-token
[script] Every tidyfeed subcommand and flag shown exists in tidyfeed/cli.py
